scope: Canonical session persistence dependency removed from direct Mongo collections through an explicit typed home SessionRepository; native real-file module acceptance only, not real API registration or login.

checks.command: corepack pnpm --dir remix run lint:files -- app/api/utils/auth/sessions.ts app/api/utils/auth/sessionCore.ts app/api/utils/auth/sessionRepository.ts app/api/utils/documentStore/nativeSessions.ts app/api/utils/documentStore/nativeSessions.test.ts app/api/utils/documentStore/collectionProvider.ts
corepack pnpm --dir remix exec tsc --noEmit --pretty false

canonicalTestWiring: test:document-store uses app/api/utils/documentStore/*.test.ts and test:unit invokes test:document-store; no package script changes needed.
covered: Actual canonical createSession/getLiveSession/revokeSession using real file-backed SQLite BSON collections.
Expiry and revocation across reopen; non-expiring session reap date; existing expiry retained; secureVaultKey removed.
Duplicate preallocated jti has one winner across two SQLite handles.
Concurrent home repository scopes remain isolated; nested/wrong-plane/expired/direct-saved repository calls refuse.
Detached or queued work after scope exit fails before writes and never falls back to Mongo.
Native caller-owned transaction options refuse before insert; no fake driver session or independent commit under a claimed caller transaction.
Existing exported Mongo revocation pipeline matches its exact historical aggregation expression/key removal contract.
Hosted canonical session helper import loads no native repository/SQLite.
Hostile session metadata accessors/toBSON hooks cannot execute before BSON admission.
mongoCompatibility: Default SessionRepository delegates to existing getSessionsCollection with identical insert options, jti filter and revokedSessionPipeline. Root owns real Mongo API harness revalidation.
limitations: No native profile/runtime/request activation selector or real HTTP registration/authenticated API acceptance.
Tests create only session records through canonical helpers; no account rows, alternate signup handler or successful authentication claim.
Caller-owned native transaction/session binding remains unsupported.
SQLite has no TTL cleanup worker; canonical live reads still enforce expiry and revocation.
Settings/rate limits, user+vault secure state, tier/subscription bootstrap, rosters, notifications, verification records and email outbox remain registration dependencies.
Provider-aware Nitro readiness/bootstrap, exact profile signing/origin, private Thing/Timeline/accounting recovery adapters and real API restart acceptance remain unfinished.
